correctness.rationale: The first n−1 coordinates identify the intrinsic torus with an (n−1)-torus. Their negative fractional parts are independent uniforms, and the last part forces their total J to be the ceiling of the first n−1 parts' sum. Cube slabs give the exact Eulerian weights, with J=1 deterministically at n=2. Subtracting the translate from each integer point leaves precisely n bounded digits in [0,t−1] summing to tk−J, so the count, coincident count atoms and occupancy interval are all handled. At t=1 the law is Bernoulli with success exactly J=k. For the mean, Haar averaging gives volume in the lattice measure (Euclidean measure divided by the root-lattice covolume √n); projecting Δ to the first n−1 coordinates gives the cube slab with sum in [k−1,k]. The ceiling shifts the sum of uniforms by at most one, so the CLT has center n/2 and asymptotic variance n/12. At either fixed-t threshold the other endpoint is separated linearly from the center; the near endpoint yields the stated Gaussian CDF with the appropriate sign. For t=2 the binomial index deviates from its center by √n(2a−Z/√12) in the limit; uniform Stirling on bounded scaled intervals and tightness give the negative quadratic limit, including −χ²₁/6 at a=0. Off center the first entropy derivative gives the stated Gaussian variance; empty events have probability tending to zero. The supplied checker.py was inspected but not executed, and the finite checks it defines are not needed for the analytic proof.
